turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you too. Thank you for seeing me. 

Um, well, I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need, but... I guess I'm here because I have a bit of trouble just staying put. It's nothing awful, really! It's just, whenever I'm supposed to sit still for a while—like during our staff meetings at work, or, you know, those briefings for church events—I get this feeling like... like there's a little motor humming right under my skin. 

I usually end up shifting around in my seat a lot, or I'll just stand in the back, or find some polite excuse to go check the hallway or something. I'm a building cleaner, so I'm used to being on my feet, and I really try hard not to be a distraction to anybody else when I do it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes shifting around in their seat a lot when expected to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient mentions standing in the back or finding excuses to leave the room during meetings where they are supposed to remain seated.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly describes a feeling of restlessness, characterized as a 'motor humming right under my skin' and having trouble staying put.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel that humming sensation under your skin, do you feel worried or anxious about the situation you are in?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, gosh, no. I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm a nervous wreck or anything! I don't feel worried at all. Actually, I'm usually perfectly happy to be there, especially at the church things. 

It's not like my mind is stressing about the meeting or... or anything bad. It's really just my body wanting to get up and do something. I just don't want you to think I'm an anxious person or that I can't handle my job, because I really can. Am I explaining that right? It's really just a physical feeling, not a worried one, if that makes sense.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a physical sensation where their body wants to get up and do something, which aligns with feeling restless.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies feeling worried or anxious, stating they are not an anxious person and do not stress about situations.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced this need to move around and this 'humming' feeling in your body since you were a child, or is this something that has only started more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Well, um... I guess it's been around for a long time. I mean, I don't want to sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I really did try to be good! But, um, I do remember back in grade school... I used to get into a little bit of trouble. Nothing serious! Just, you know, popping out of my seat when I wasn't supposed to, or maybe talking over the teacher sometimes. 

I'd also sort of rush ahead and start things before all the directions were finished. I just got so eager, I suppose. My mother used to tell people I acted like I was wound a little too tight, even back then. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terror to deal with. I really did want to please my teachers and my parents. Does that answer your question okay?

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient confirms the doctor's description of having a need to move around and a 'humming' feeling since childhood.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient notes their mother described them as acting like they were 'wound a little too tight', indicating constant activity or being driven by a motor.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient mentions 'talking over the teacher sometimes', which is a form of interrupting or intruding on others.

turns.doctor_question: When you are working or doing other tasks, do you find that your mind tends to wander or that you struggle to keep your focus on the task at hand?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, sir. Um... not at all, really. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging or anything, but I actually focus pretty well! I'm a very hard worker, I promise. 

When I have a job to do at work, like buffing the floors or clearing out the offices, I just get right to it and stay on track. My mind doesn't really drift off or go daydreaming. I don't lose track of what I'm doing. It's really just the opposite, I suppose—I like to keep moving and get things done, so as long as I have a task in front of me, I'm completely tuned into it. 

I don't really struggle with the attention part of things at all. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being helpful.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient denies that their mind drifts off or goes daydreaming while working.

turns.doctor_question: When you are lying in bed at night trying to fall asleep, do you ever feel that same 'humming' or uncomfortable sensation in your legs that makes you feel like you need to move them to get relief?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, I don't think so. I really hope I'm not confusing things, but no, I don't get that feeling when I'm trying to sleep. 

Once I'm in bed, I'm usually out like a light! I work pretty hard during the day, so by the time my head hits the pillow, I'm just ready to rest. My legs don't bother me or feel restless at all at night. I sleep just fine, I promise. I don't want you to think I have trouble sleeping or anything like that. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
